newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe secret service chief goes blind - paper.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe secret service chief goes blind - paper.

text.p: Zimbabwe's intelligence services chief has been blinded by a rare blood disease, but President Robert Mugabe has allowed him to run the feared organisation for a whole year despite this handicap, the independent Financial Gazette reported on Thursday.

Elleck Mashingaidze, director-general of the Central Intelligence Organisation (CIO), was unavailable for comment and government officials refused to discuss the story which the newspaper attributed to authoritative security sources.

The weekly Financial Gazette said Mashingaidze, CIO head since 1991, lost his eyesight this year. It had started to deteriorate in 1995 when the former diplomat suffered a rare blood disease which the paper did not name.

"He can't see and we are reading every document for him, including newspapers," it quoted a senior CIO agent as saying, adding there were fears Zimbabwe's national security might be compromised by this arrangement.
The CIO boss was learning to use a braille machine to read and write, it said.

Mashingaidze served Zimbabwe as its ambassador to the United Nations in the early 1980s and also as secretary in the ministry of foreign affairs before his appointment to the CIO, which in the 1980s and early 90s was accused of human rights violations.
